2010.2.1.description:
Hosts/Routers MUST silently discard IP packets with version not equal to 4

[Log-derived analysis] Hosts/Routers MUST silently discard IP packets with version not equal to 4
2010.2.1.reference: RFC 1812 IP Header Validation s5.2.2 p67 RFC 1122 Requirements for Internet Hosts s3.2.1.1 p29

2010.2.2.description:
Hosts/Routers MUST silently discard IP packets with bad checksum

[Log-derived analysis] Hosts/Routers MUST silently discard IP packets with bad checksum
2010.2.2.reference: RFC 1812 IP Header Validation s5.2.2 p67 RFC 1122 Requirements for Internet Hosts s3.2.1.1 p29

2010.2.3.description:
Hosts/Routers MUST NOT discard IP packets with TTL delivered locally

[Log-derived analysis] Hosts/Routers MUST NOT discard IP packets with TTL delivered locally
2010.2.3.reference: RFC 1812 Time To Live s4.2.2.9 p46 RFC 1122 Requirements for Internet Hosts s3.2.1.7 p34

2010.2.5.description:
A router MUST NOT set unused (reserved) bits to one in datagrams originated by the router

[Log-derived analysis] A router MUST NOT set unused (reserved) bits to one in datagrams originated by the router
2010.2.5.reference: RFC 1812 Unused IP Header Bits s4.2.2.3 p43

2010.2.6.description:
A router MUST NOT drop a packet merely because one or more of the reserved bits has a non-zero value

[Log-derived analysis] A router MUST NOT drop a packet merely because one or more of the reserved bits has a non-zero value
2010.2.6.reference: RFC 1812 Unused IP Header Bits s4.2.2.3 p43

2010.2.7.description:
A router MUST ignore IP options which it does not recognize. A router MUST implement the 'End of Option List' and 'No Operation' options

[Log-derived analysis] A router MUST ignore IP options which it does not recognize. A router MUST implement the 'End of Option List' and 'No Operation' options
2010.2.7.reference: RFC 1812 Unrecognized Header Options s4.2.2.6 p44

2010.2.9.description:
Router MUST silently discard datagram with bad destination IP address

[Log-derived analysis] Router MUST silently discard datagram with bad destination IP address
2010.2.9.reference: RFC 1812 Addressing s4.2.2.11 p48 RFC 1812 IP Broadcast Addresses s4.2.3.1 p50

2010.2.10.description:
Router MUST Silently discard datagram with bad source IP address

[Inferred behavior — case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] Router MUST Silently discard datagram with bad source IP address

2010.3.1.description:
The TTL for ICMP responses must not be taken from the packet which triggered the response

[Log-derived analysis] The TTL for ICMP responses must not be taken from the packet which triggered the response
2010.3.1.reference: RFC 1812 ICMP Message TTL s4.3.2.2 p53

2010.3.2.description:
The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request

[Log-derived analysis] The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request

2010.3.3.description:
A router SHOULD NOT respond to ICMP Information Request messages

[Log-derived analysis] A router SHOULD NOT respond to ICMP Information Request messages

2010.3.4.description:
A router MUST implement support for responding to ICMP Address Mask request messages

[Inferred behavior — case reported UNSUPPORTED on the current test setup; no recent PASS] A router MUST implement support for responding to ICMP Address Mask request messages
2010.3.4.reference: RFC 1812 Address Mask Request/Reply s4.3.3.9 p61

2010.4.1.description:
IP packets with invalid headers MUST be discarded

[Log-derived analysis] IP packets with invalid headers MUST be discarded
2010.4.1.reference: RFC 1812 IP Header Validation s5.2.2 p67

2010.4.2.description:
A router MUST generate an ICMP Time Exceeded message when it discards a packet due to an expired TTL field

[Log-derived analysis] A router MUST generate an ICMP Time Exceeded message when it discards a packet due to an expired TTL field

2010.5.1.description:
When a router forwards a packet, it MUST reduce the TTL by at least 1

[Log-derived analysis] When a router forwards a packet, it MUST reduce the TTL by at least 1
2010.5.1.reference: RFC 1812 Time to Live (TTL) s5.3.1 p85
